unit.title: Angles
unit.blurb: Comparing angles, right angles, acute and obtuse angles, and estimating the size of angles in degrees.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Compare angles with a right angle and order angles by size.

O2.t: Classify angles as acute, right or obtuse.

O3.t: Estimate the size of angles in degrees.

p: An **angle** is an amount of turn. A **right angle** is a quarter turn, **90°**. A straight line is two right angles, **180°**.
To compare angles, look at how far one arm turns from the other – not at how long the arms are.
Longer arms do not make a bigger angle.

p: Use angles you know to estimate: **90°** (right angle), **45°** (half a right angle), **180°** (straight line).
An angle a bit less than a right angle might be about 80°; halfway between 90° and 180° is about 135°.
If an angle is obtuse, your estimate must be more than 90°.
